contexts.text: As the celestial man is the Lord's... it is not conceded to him to possess these things as his own.
Whatever is with the worldly and corporeal man, he calls his own...
All Spirits appear constantly in their own places.
It is the Celestial of love not to want to be one's own; but to belong to all; so that it wants to give all things which are its own to others...
Disposes (the Natural) as its own.
Every man (then) thinks that the good and truth from which he combats are his own...
What is the Lord's he makes his own.
When anyone worships the Lord from non-freedom, he worships from nothing of his own.
Nothing appears to man as his own; or, what is the same, as his proprium; than that which flows from freedom. Explained.
For man perceives nothing else in himself than what is his own...
Thus man makes evils his own, or proper to him.
For the truths which had appeared to him as his own, when goods were conjoined, were apperceived as if taken away. Explained. AC 4151:2.

No one has any good and truth which are his own... but still it appears as if good and truth were his own; and this for the reason that they may be appropriated to man, until he comes into such a state that he knows, then acknowledges, and at last believes, that they are not his, but the Lord's.
Theft = ... when it attributes to itself, and makes its own, the goods and truths...
The man who is being regenerated, is at last so far reduced... that he no longer wants to be his own, but the Lord's.
The Lord... wills a total submission, that is, that man should not be partly his own, and partly the Lord's. Explained.
It is proper to love that all its own be from itself in others.
He who loves himself, loves also those who belong to him... whom he calls his own.
This freedom... together with life, is given to man as his own...
To love what is one's own... in another, disjoins...
Who can want to be wise, unless he feels and perceives that which he loves, learns, and imbibes, as his own? Who can otherwise retain it? Explained.
How an angel perceives and feels as his own; and thus receives and retains; when yet it is not his for an Angel is not an Angel from what is his own... Explained.
That the more closely man is conjoined with the Lord, the more distinctly he appears to himself as if he is his own... General article.
Whatever man thinks, wills, speaks, and does, from freedom, he perceives as his own...
For anything to which anyone is compelled does not appear as his own; and that which does not appear as his own cannot become of his love, and so be appropriated to him as his own.
How can man claim for himself what is Divine merely because these few outermost things appear to him as his own?
Intelligence appears as his own and proper to him both with a good man and an evil one...

Whatever man acts from the will as his own according to the understanding as his own... remains permanently. By this the Lord brings man into a state of conjunction with Himself; and in this He reforms, regenerates, and saves him.
This is what is meant by... being gathered to their own. AE 659:17, Explained.
This is given to man as his own...
